figures.name: Matching colours connect each glyph, its Unicode number and all its UTF-8 bytes. Read each column downward: four Unicode numbers occupy five byte positions.
The cyan payload cells carry é's number. Neutral prefix cells identify the start and continuation bytes; each completed row has eight bits.
Colour follows each byte value through all three rows; brackets mark groups. Four byte cells keep their order: the middle token contains the tail of one scalar and the start of another.
Matching é hues identify both spellings and their common glyph. Two distinct scalar/byte paths converge at NFC; the common output cannot identify which spelling was supplied.
Bracket hues follow each learned piece; byte-cell hues keep their glyph correspondence. The same five byte columns remain aligned through four merge ranks; no byte is removed.
A decoder starts ready, remembers a partial scalar, and emits only after its payload is complete. Invalid input or an incomplete final flush leaves this strict path with an error.
Byte C3 selects ID 198, an address into the amber learned table. The white outlined row becomes a computed vector; contextual processing produces one score per next-ID choice.
Matching hues follow a byte value or control symbol across the shifted rows. Read each column as one next-step decision: the target is one place ahead; EOS follows the complete byte spelling.
The A and é rows share width three. Causal connections exclude the future; the shorter row also has a PAD key and a separate ignored PAD target.
Both bars use probability 0–1. Violet is the same correct A9 target in each; the rest is probability on other IDs.

Matching glyph colours recur in the input and output byte prefixes. Computed feature grids stay violet: the decoder consults encoder features while generating output bytes, with causal connections between output decisions.

CANINE hashes Unicode code points into learned bucket embeddings, combines them, shortens local feature positions for the deep encoder, then restores character resolution with fine-feature information.

Two candidate block spans over the same byte sequence contribute weighted vectors. Candidate features and weights are constructed for this exact mixing example; GBST learns block scores before downsampling.

The recurrent-state path carries learned context between bytes. A new byte enters each state update; its contextual output produces the next-byte scores. Circles depict states, not attention to every earlier byte.

Matching hues follow patch identity from bytes to feature rows, global vectors and decoder context; scores remain violet. The decoder receives completed earlier-patch context plus causal current-prefix features. This draws availability, not the full BLT mask configuration.
Constructed probabilities before the next byte. Each full bar is 100%; the violet and neutral portions are the two labelled candidates. No observed outcome enters this entropy calculation.
Three constructed two-entry vectors become one two-entry mean. Wires combine corresponding entries; grouping reduces the number of positions while feature width stays two.
Every allowed relationship occupies the same-sized violet cell. The smaller global grid has six rather than 36 pairs; local byte work is outside these grids.
The same ten original UTF-8 bytes supply both likelihood denominators. Model positions may differ; their total negative log likelihood is compared per shared byte unit.

All four blue byte decisions belong to the same globe glyph; they still form a serial chain. A block decoder scores several unknown positions in one call, possibly over repeated refinements. This is a qualitative dependency picture, not timing or a trained output.
